messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — I just finished a cross-GPU seq/batch sweep for the new attention kernel policy (flash-fused, paged-flash, fallback). Results look odd on H100: intermittent latency microbursts when seq >= 4096 with batch=2. Repro steps and raw profiler below.

ryan: hmm, microbursts? are we talking kernel switchbacks between flash and fallback?

maya: yep. the selector toggles back and forth mid-request in a few cases. seems tied to kvcache prefetch/kvcache eviction patterns. logged a few samples.

maya: command I ran: ```
# run sweep (A100/H100/L40S)
./bench/attn_sweep --gpus A100,H100,L40S --seq-lens 512,1024,2048,4096,8192 --batches 1,2,4 --kernels flash_fused,paged_flash,fallback --runs 3 --save-json /tmp/attn_sweep.json
```

maya: profiler snippet (H100, seq=4096, batch=2, run#2):
```
timestamp: 1769998888
kernel_sample: flash_fused  avg_ms_per_token=2.12  p90=2.50
kernel_sample: paged_flash  avg_ms_per_token=3.78  p90=4.10
kernel_sample: fallback_matmul  avg_ms_per_token=11.9  p90=12.4
selector: initial=flash_fused -> paged_flash -> flash_fused (switch_count=18)
kvcache: prefetch_hits=1204  prefetch_misses=78  evictions=26
end
```

sam: Do you have the selector config? maybe the hysteresis window is too small and we oscillate when the instantaneous seq distribution changes.

maya: snippet from selector config used: ```
selector.policy: hybrid
thresholds:
  flash_min_seq: 256
  flash_max_seq: 8192
  hysteresis_ms: 8   # current value
  kvcache_prefetch_threshold: 0.15
  kvcache_eviction_backoff_ms: 120
```

jess: 8ms hysteresis seems small for the H100 microbursting we saw last month. Try 30-50ms? also verify prefetch depth for paged_flash.

maya: bumping hysteresis to 40ms locally reduced switch_count from ~18 -> 2 for that sample, latencies stabilized (p90 down ~23%). will run full sweep.

perf-bot: Jenkins run #attn-sweep-1769 finished: artifacts at https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/attn/1769998888 (contains full json + perf traces).

ryan: good. also check kv-cache affinity — if requests get pinned to different CUDA contexts after a fallback, we could be thrashing memory and invalidating KV pages, causing delays.

maya: found this in logs during the spikes: ```
WARN kvcache: eviction triggered, victim_size=1.2MB, ctx_switch=true
DEBUG runtime: kernel_switchback triggered by mem_pressure=0.82 gpu_util=97
```

sam: That ctx_switch flag is worrying. Maybe our prefetch threads are on a different NVLink path and eviction causes page migration. Can you repro with `--affinity=pin`?

maya: scheduled a focused run with --affinity=pin and hysteresis=40ms. preliminary: H100 spikes go away, A100 unaffected. L40S shows slight improvement.

infra-bot: GPU metrics during run (H100): mem_used=38.6GB/80GB, gpu_util=95-99% during bursts, nvlink_latency avg=0.9ms peaks 4.6ms correlated with spike windows.

jess: action items:
- maya: finish full sweep with pinned affinity + hysteresis=40ms, upload traces (ETA 2h)
- sam: add a selector test that simulates ctx switches and asserts switch_count < 3 for seq>=2048
- ryan: follow up on kvcache prefetch placement (threading/affinity)

maya: noted. I'll also try an experiment where paged_flash prefetch depth is lowered to make it less aggressive (kvcache_prefetch_threshold -> 0.10) and see impact on p99 tail.

sam: thanks — if that fixes it we can roll a soft rollout (10% of requests on H100 clusters) and watch tail metrics in Console. :eyes:

maya: uploaded initial artifacts and a short flamegraph in the CI link. leaving logs here for quick debug: ```
# small excerpt of request timeline (events):
0ms: request start -> kernel=flash_fused
1.1ms: kvcache prefetch start
1.6ms: kernel switch -> paged_flash (prefetch miss)
6.9ms: eviction + ctx_switch logged
12.0ms: fallback_matmul executed (big spike)
end
```

perf-bot: noted new regression ticket: PERF-4127 created and linked to this thread.

ryan: solid. prioritize reproducer + selector unit test before any rollout.

maya: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
